title: Module quiz: Claude in the software life cycle

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team wants its own rules about money handling and generated files applied only when pull requests are checked, and not in ordinary sessions. Which file holds them?

options.text: `CLAUDE.md`, which every session reads before its first prompt
options.says: Ruled out because `CLAUDE.md` is "shared project instructions that Claude Code uses for all tasks, not just reviews".

options.text: `REVIEW.md`, read by the agents that examine the diff
options.says: The page says `REVIEW.md` holds "review-only instructions", and that you use it "to say what your team wants flagged, at what severity, and how findings are reported".

options.text: `.claude/settings.json`, which the whole team commits to the repository
options.says: Ruled out because the first page gives that file "Team permission rules, default model, hooks, plugins", which are settings and not review instructions.

options.text: `prompts/CHANGELOG.md`, which lists the prompt versions and their dates
options.says: Ruled out because the changelog explains versions of prompts, and the first page says it must have "A changelog entry for every change" and not review rules.

questions.stem: A prompt file is at version 1.2.0, and its changelog's newest heading says 1.1.0. What does a reviewer conclude?

options.text: The edit is unrecorded, because the record and the number disagree
options.says: The first page says the changelog's "latest heading equals the file's version", so a mismatch means a change nobody recorded.

options.text: The prompt is older than its record, so it should be reverted at once
options.says: Ruled out because the rule is only a heading that is "whose latest heading equals the file's version", and it names no age comparison.

options.text: The number is wrong, because the record always wins out in such a case
options.says: Ruled out because the only rule is "whose latest heading equals the file's version", with no winner, so a reviewer asks for the missing entry.

options.text: Nothing, because the changelog is only for people to read
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "A reviewer reading the pull request sees what changed and why", which makes it part of the review.

questions.stem: A job must start only for a new note that names the bot, and a second note on the same issue must not stop work that is running. Which pair of settings fits?

options.text: A guard on the comment body, with `cancel-in-progress` set to false
options.says: The page says to guard the job with `if: contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude')`, and for an implementation run to "leave it `false` so that a second comment does not kill work in progress."

options.text: No guard on the comment body, with `cancel-in-progress` set to true
options.says: Ruled out because "Without the `if`, a runner starts for every comment in the repository".

options.text: A guard on the comment body, with `cancel-in-progress` set to true
options.says: Ruled out because `cancel-in-progress: true` suits a review: "so a new push replaces the review of an outdated commit".

options.text: No guard on the comment body, with `cancel-in-progress` set to false
options.says: Ruled out because it lacks the guard, and "Without the `if`, a runner starts for every comment in the repository".

questions.stem: A team must choose how to run a nightly dependency review that keeps working when nobody's laptop is on, with no workflow in the repository. Which option fits?

options.text: A hook in the settings file that fires after each edit
options.says: Ruled out because hooks are among the things the shared settings file holds, "Team permission rules, default model, hooks, plugins", and they run inside a session on a machine, while a routine keeps working "while your laptop is closed".

options.text: A mention workflow that waits for someone to comment
options.says: Ruled out because "its job starts only when the comment mentions the bot", and the job here is nightly.

options.text: A routine with a scheduled trigger on Anthropic's cloud
options.says: The page says a routine is "a saved Claude Code configuration", with a scheduled trigger, and it runs on cloud infrastructure so it keeps working "while your laptop is closed".

options.text: A subagent in the project folder that starts at midnight
options.says: Ruled out because subagents are files the repository lists as "Team skills and subagents", which a session loads when it starts, so nothing starts one at midnight, and only a routine "is a saved Claude Code configuration" that runs "automatically".
